strengths: Conceptual Motivation: Framing self-attention dynamics through the lens of Krause bounded-confidence consensus models provides an intuitive and conceptually appealing perspective on multi-cluster representation preservation and attention sink mitigation.

Comprehensive Experimental Breadth: The authors evaluate the proposed Krause Attention across three distinct paradigms—vision recognition (ViT and Swin backbones), autoregressive image generation, and large language models (Llama-3 and Qwen1.5)—showing consistent improvements and efficiency benefits.

Computational Efficiency: Combining local windowing with top-k selective sparsity provides a concrete sub-quadratic complexity ($O(NWd)$), leading to measurable FLOP reductions in vision models and inference speedups in autoregressive generation.

Thorough Appendix and Ablations: The manuscript includes detailed ablations on local windows, sparsity, and kernel distance formulation (e.g., Table 13 and Table 16), as well as visualizations of attention map diversity across layers.
weaknesses: Theoretical Analysis Relies on Strong Assumptions: The theoretical results in Appendix C (both continuous-time particle dynamics and mean-field Wasserstein flow) crucially assume that the token representations are already partitioned into well-separated clusters beyond the interaction radius $R$ ($\inf \|Qx - Ky\| > R$). Consequently, block-diagonal decoupling and independent cluster convergence become immediate algebraic consequences of the hard cutoff, rather than a proof that multi-clustering dynamically emerges from arbitrary initial configurations under layered feedforward networks.

Confounding Locality Bias on Small Image Datasets: Standard ViTs trained from scratch on small datasets like CIFAR-10/100 suffer notoriously from the lack of 2D inductive bias. Constraining attention to a local spatial grid (such as a 4-neighbor window) inherently introduces strong local priors similar to convolutions. While Table 14 attempts to isolate this on SwinTransformers, the performance delta on Swin is much smaller (+0.36% on Swin-T, +0.92% on Swin-S) compared to vanilla ViT (+8.27% on ViT-T on CIFAR-100), suggesting that standard spatial locality accounts for a major portion of the observed gains.

LLM Evaluation Setup and Baselines: In LLMs, Krause Attention is introduced as an auxiliary shortcut pathway alongside standard attention rather than a replacement. The LoRA comparison is slightly confounded because Krause-LLM adds an extra attention pathway and introduces additional trainable parameters (0.59% vs 0.52% overhead). A more rigorous baseline would compare against an equivalent auxiliary standard attention or convolutional/local shortcut of identical capacity.

Degenerative Generation in Qualitative Examples: In Table 21 (IFEval qualitative outputs), both the baseline LoRA model and Krause-Llama-3-8B exhibit severe degenerative looping/repetition across sentences. While Krause-LLM alters the content, the presence of repetitive loops raises questions about generation quality under free-form instruction following.

strengths: Principled motivation connecting dynamical systems (Krause bounded-confidence consensus, interacting particle systems) to Transformer self-attention, providing an intuitive conceptual framework for mitigating global synchronization and representational collapse.

Theoretical grounding in Appendix C adapting recent continuous-time and mean-field Wasserstein gradient-flow frameworks (Geshkovski et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2025) to explain the emergence and stability of multi-cluster equilibria under bounded-confidence interactions.

Extensive experimental evaluation across three distinct domains and modalities: vision recognition (ViT and Swin on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1K, Fashion-MNIST), generative modeling (autoregressive image generation on MNIST and CIFAR-10), and language reasoning (Llama3-8B and Qwen1.5-7B).
Solid empirical investigation into attention sinks (Figures 7, 11), demonstrating that localizing interactions effectively dampens disproportionate attention mass allocation on initial tokens.
Comprehensive ablation studies (Section D.2.3, D.3.2) dissecting the effects of the RBF kernel, spatial/causal local windowing, and top-k selection under varying data augmentation conditions.
weaknesses: Equivalence to softmax with key-norm bias: The unnormalized RBF score is $s_{i,j} = \exp(-\|q_i - k_j\|^2 / (2\sigma^2)) = \exp(-\|q_i\|^2 / 2\sigma^2) \exp(-\|k_j\|^2 / 2\sigma^2) \exp(q_i^T k_j / \sigma^2)$. When normalized over candidates $j$, the query norm $\exp(-\|q_i\|^2 / 2\sigma^2)$ factors out and cancels in the numerator and denominator. Consequently, Krause attention is functionally equivalent to standard softmax attention with temperature $\sigma^2$ and an additive key-norm penalty $-\|k_j\|^2 / (2\sigma^2)$. The manuscript claims that it avoids softmax normalization, which is technically misleading since row-normalization of exponentials is the softmax operator.

Divergence from classical Krause dynamics: In classical Krause consensus, bounded confidence is defined strictly in the state/feature space (i.e., $|x_i - x_j| \le \epsilon$). In the proposed architecture, the primary bounding mechanism $\mathcal{N}_i$ is enforced over spatial pixel coordinates or causal temporal sequence positions, rather than solely representation distance. The role of 'bounded confidence' thus heavily relies on standard spatial/temporal local windowing combined with top-k selection.

Suboptimal ImageNet-1K baselines: In Table 3, ViT-S-16 achieves 74.04% and ViT-B-16 achieves 72.19% after 300 epochs. Standard DeiT recipes typically achieve ~79.8% (Small) and ~81.8% (Base). The fact that ViT-B performs worse than ViT-S suggests optimization or hyperparameter under-tuning for the baselines, weakening the decisiveness of the ImageNet gains.

Confounding factors in LLM evaluation: In the LLM experiments (Section 5.4), Krause Attention is incorporated as an auxiliary shortcut pathway with a learnable mixing ratio and trained with additional LoRA parameters (0.59% vs. 0.52% for baseline). To demonstrate that the gains are specifically due to Krause dynamics rather than simply adding a dual-attention parallel branch or extra capacity, an ablation baseline featuring an auxiliary standard local-attention shortcut with identical parameterization is needed.

Practical wall-clock training throughput: While theoretical FLOPs and autoregressive generation throughput on small resolutions are reported, gathering top-k elements dynamically within local windows often introduces memory non-coalescence and kernel launch overheads on modern hardware. Wall-clock training throughput and GPU memory benchmarks for full training runs (e.g., ViT on ImageNet) are not reported.

strengths: Conceptual Motivation: Framing self-attention dynamics through the lens of Hegselmann-Krause bounded-confidence consensus models offers an interesting perspective on representation collapse and token clustering.

Broad Experimental Scope: The paper evaluates the proposed Krause Attention across three distinct domains: Vision Transformers (CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1K), autoregressive image generation (MNIST, CIFAR-10), and decoder-only LLMs (Llama-3-8B and Qwen1.5-7B).

Comprehensive Ablations: The authors provide extensive ablation studies in the appendix (Tables 13, 15, and 16) analyzing the decoupled contributions of the RBF kernel, local windowing, and top-k sparsification.
weaknesses: Conceptual Disconnect Between Krause Consensus and Implementation: In classical Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, clustering emerges endogenously because agents only interact if their states are within a confidence radius in representation space. In contrast, the primary driver of bounded interactions in this work is a hard, predefined coordinate-space window (e.g., a 4-neighbor spatial grid in vision, or a causal window of 32 tokens in language) combined with a heuristic top-k selection. The similarity to bounded confidence is largely metaphorical, as the mechanism heavily relies on standard sliding-window and top-k sparse attention techniques.

Conditional Theoretical Analysis: The theoretical arguments in Appendix C do not demonstrate that multi-cluster formation spontaneously emerges from general initial conditions under learned transformations. Instead, the proofs assume a priori that the token representations are already partitioned into well-separated clusters outside each other's interaction radius (Eq. 14 and Eq. 25). Showing that disconnected blocks in an attention matrix remain disconnected is algebraically immediate and does not resolve the open question of how such clusters form dynamically during training.

Confounding Experimental Setups in LLM Evaluations: In the LLM experiments (Section 5.4), Krause Attention is not evaluated as a replacement for standard self-attention, but rather as an additional parallel pathway with extra projection parameters (QK, KK, VK, OK projs, Table 11) blended into the residual stream via LoRA. The observed gains on downstream reasoning tasks could stem from increased model capacity, dual-pathway ensembling, or additional trainable parameters, rather than the bounded-confidence prior specifically.

Trivialized Mitigation of Attention Sinks: The paper claims Krause Attention mitigates the 'attention sink' phenomenon (Figure 7 and Section 5.4). However, when a causal window of size 32 is enforced, tokens past position 32 are mechanically prohibited from attending to token 0 because it falls outside the receptive window. Alleviating attention sinks by strictly truncating attention distance via a local sliding window is an expected consequence of windowed attention rather than an emergent property of consensus dynamics.

Suboptimal Baselines and Locality Bias in Vision Tasks: Training standard ViTs from scratch on small datasets like CIFAR-10/100 without pretraining is known to suffer significantly from a lack of spatial inductive bias. Imposing a 4-neighbor spatial window trivially provides this local bias, which is why local attention and convolutions outperform vanilla ViTs in this regime. Furthermore, on ImageNet-1K (Table 3), the reported ViT-B-16 baseline of 72.19% is considerably lower than established standard training recipes (e.g., DeiT reaches 81.8%), indicating undertuned baselines.
